notes:
One state, two Cliopatria rows: the Zhou royal house ran from 1046 to 256 BC; Cliopatria's 'Zhou Dynasty' row (-1000..-751) is the Western Zhou plus twenty Eastern Zhou years, and its 'Later Zhou' row (-750..960, owned by another ea-01 batch) is the Eastern Zhou plus the Five Dynasties Later Zhou. This dossier ends at Cliopatria's handoff (751) with a 'dissolve' to eastern-zhou (suggested slug) so that the map has no gap; the real events are the 771 loss of the Wei valley, the move to Wangcheng and the rename to Eastern Zhou, all in the ledger. The reviewer may instead merge the two into one zhou-dynasty dossier (rule 2), in which case this file's ledger stands and the Later Zhou shapes -750..-256 need review.

Cliopatria rows to correct: the Zhou start 1000 should be 1046 (new keyframe); the Shang end 1001 should be 1046; the whole 700,000 km2 is drawn as direct rule where only the royal domain was (vassal tint for the fengjian states).

Vassals: vassal_start events are written only for the five fiefs whose pages were opened (Song, Cao, Cai, Chen, Chu); Jin, Qi, Lu, Wey, Zheng, Yan, Qin, Xu, Teng and Zhu were fiefs too but the Zhou and Western Zhou pages name none of them (Qi only as 'a state originally founded by one of King Wu's generals'), so their dossiers' pages should supply the dates (gap). The vassal_end events at 751 are a data handoff, confidence 1; the allegiance was nominal through the Spring and Autumn period.

Counterparts without a Cliopatria row: the Quanrong (took the Wei valley in 771; the Rong and Di are in the ea-01-x scope), the Xianyun, the Huaiyi, Shen (the Marquis of Shen), Wu Geng's Shang remnant. The Wei valley passes to Qin in Cliopatria from 750; the pages opened do not record the grant to Duke Xiang of Qin.

Dates: the Zhou page gives 1046 (Chronology Project) and 1045 (Shaughnessy) for Muye; the Zhou page moves the capital in 771, the Western Zhou page leaves the move undated; the Three Guards' rebellion and the Shandong campaign are undated on both pages (1042-1040 inferred from King Cheng's accession). No infobox area on either page; Cliopatria's 699,623 km2 is unchecked.
